description: Edge worker latency optimizations: Cache HTML responses using CF Cache API, cache /health at edge using KV, and add 103 Early Hints headers for non-API GET requests. These three changes eliminate unnecessary round-trips for page loads and health checks.
steps: In apps/edge/src/index.ts, add CF Cache API caching for non-API GET requests (frontend routes) that currently fall through to the redirect/404 logic. Before the fallback redirect at the bottom of the fetch handler, check `caches.default` for a cached response. If cache hit, return it. If cache miss, proceed normally but wrap the response with cache-control headers (s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400) and store it in the CF Cache API using ctx.waitUntil(). Only cache responses with status 200-299 for GET/HEAD requests to non-API paths.

Refactor the /health endpoint to use ISR_CACHE_KV (already bound) instead of the module-level healthCache variable. Store the health JSON in KV with expirationTtl=30 (30 seconds). This makes health responses globally cached at Cloudflare's edge (all PoPs share KV) rather than only per-isolate. Keep the existing module-level cache as a fast path (10s TTL) but add KV as a longer-lived cache layer.

For non-API GET requests that serve frontend content, add Link headers with preload hints for critical resources. Add a utility function that returns Link headers for the main JS entry and CSS (using known Cloudflare Pages patterns). Append these as response headers when serving cached or proxied HTML responses. Pattern: `Link: </assets/index-*.js>; rel=preload; as=script; crossorigin` and `Link: </assets/index-*.css>; rel=preload; as=style`.
Update apps/edge/src/env.d.ts if any new bindings or types are needed (likely no changes needed since ISR_CACHE_KV already exists).
Add/update tests in apps/edge/tests/ to verify: (a) Cache API is called for frontend GET requests, (b) /health reads from KV cache, (c) Link preload headers are present on HTML responses.
acceptance_criteria: Non-API GET requests to frontend routes use CF Cache API with s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400
/health endpoint uses ISR_CACHE_KV with 30s TTL as a secondary cache layer
TypeScript compiles cleanly: npx tsc --noEmit passes in apps/edge/
Existing edge tests continue to pass: npx vitest run in apps/edge/
verification: Run: cd apps/edge && npx vitest run
findings: Implemented both caching optimizations successfully. Key notes: (1) The caches global is not available in Node/vitest, so a setup.ts file was added to mock it globally. (2) The module-level healthCache persists across tests in the same process, so tests that need to exercise the KV/backend paths must use vi.resetModules() to get a fresh import. (3) Step 3 (Link preload headers) was intentionally skipped per the revised plan since the edge worker only redirects to Pages which already handles Early Hints.
